violations.description: Unrestored environment variable. The client fixture calls create_app, and create_app calls telemetry.instrument_app, which calls set_semconv_opt_in and writes os.environ['OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN']. The autouse guard in tests/unit/conftest.py:29-32 calls monkeypatch.delenv(opt_in, raising=False) when the variable is absent. pytest's MonkeyPatch.delitem records an undo only when the key exists, so the guard registers nothing and the value set by the first test stays for the rest of the session. A per-test snapshot plugin, run read-only from outside the repo across the full local suite (725 passed), confirmed it: 'tests/unit/test_app.py::test_best_match: env OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN: None -> gen_ai_latest_experimental,database,http' was the only environment, logger, cwd, sys.path, OTel-provider or instrumentation change any test left behind. Which test leaks depends on order. Any test that calls create_app, load.main, migrate.main or telemetry.setup leaks when it runs first, and every later test sees the variable already set. test_telemetry.py:296 and test_telemetry_expanded.py:439 already clear it defensively because of this.
violations.recommendation: In tests/unit/conftest.py, register the undo even when the variable is absent. For example, monkeypatch.setenv(opt_in, 'x') then monkeypatch.delenv(opt_in), or save os.environ.get(opt_in) and restore or pop it in the finally block. The tests themselves need no change.
violations.suggestion: In tests/unit/conftest.py, register the undo even when the variable is absent. For example, monkeypatch.setenv(opt_in, 'x') then monkeypatch.delenv(opt_in), or save os.environ.get(opt_in) and restore or pop it in the finally block. The tests themselves need no change.
violations.code_snippet:
else:
    monkeypatch.delenv(opt_in, raising=False)  # conftest.py:32: absent key -> no undo recorded

violations.description: The module-level mutable cache _TRACE_ID: list[str] = [] is filled inside a test through _traced_search() and never reset. test_one_search_yields_one_trace_in_tempo (8) and test_the_trace_is_served_by_grafanas_tempo_datasource (8b) share one trace id. When 8 runs first, 8b reuses its id and does not make its own search. If 8 has already recorded an id whose trace never arrives, 8b fails on the same id instead of checking Grafana independently. Run on its own or first, 8b makes the search itself. Test order therefore changes what 8b exercises and whether it can pass. This was reviewed statically because the kind tests are deselected locally.
violations.recommendation: Use a module-scoped pytest fixture, for example `@pytest.fixture(scope='module') def traced_search_id() -> str: return _search_with_traceparent()`, or call _search_with_traceparent() in each test. The sharing then belongs to the fixture lifecycle instead of a mutable global that never resets.
violations.suggestion: Use a module-scoped pytest fixture, for example `@pytest.fixture(scope='module') def traced_search_id() -> str: return _search_with_traceparent()`, or call _search_with_traceparent() in each test. The sharing then belongs to the fixture lifecycle instead of a mutable global that never resets.
